display_name: Retire the lanes whose work is provably finished
description: Drive every named managed_session whose own assigned Unit is proved terminal in the project-solet register to lifecycle_state retired, through the existing retire_session verb and nothing else. The gap this closes: the lane worktree sweep only ever considers paths derived from managed_session rows already terminated or retired, and protects every row in spawning, live, idle, overdue or parked, so a lane whose Unit finished long ago but whose ledger row is still live, idle or overdue is invisible to disposal twice over - it is never retired, and its tree is protected from the sweep. For each given instance this verb resolves that row's own stored, digest-verified assignment (never an inferred Unit), reads that Unit's current state through the same read-only register CLI boundary a retirement already uses for custody evidence, and where the state is one the register itself treats as terminal (accepted, completed, cancelled, superseded, abandoned) calls retire_session unchanged. Every effect on a host is retire_session's: its five steps in fixed order, its adjudication of the lane worktree before the irreversible host termination, its proof-based removal of that tree afterwards, and its refusal to delete bytes it cannot prove recoverable. This verb adds no termination mechanism, no disposal rule and no lifecycle state of its own. Proof is positive and required: only a register read that completed for the exact assigned Unit and returned a terminal state makes a row eligible. A row with no registered assignment, a read that did not complete, a Unit still in flight, or a retire_session that declined that row is left exactly as it was - ledger state and worktree both - and reported as one advisory naming the row and the reason, while the remaining rows continue. Nothing here refuses and the caller is never failed because one row could not be proved; unknown is never treated as completed, because retiring a lane is irreversible for its host. Idempotent and re-drivable: a row already retired is a cheap no-op through retire_session's own already-retired early return and costs no register read, so calling this twice leaves the same end state. considered counts the rows read. retired carries one record per row driven through retire_session, with its unit_id, the unit_state that proved it, already_retired, the resulting lifecycle_state and the worktree_disposition the ledger recorded; unit_state is empty for an already-retired row, where no register read was made. advisories carries one string per untouched row. An agent_instance_id that names no managed_session row is refused as session_not_found, exactly as retire_session refuses it.
embedding_description: Retire the managed lanes whose work is finished: for each named session this checks that session's own assigned Unit in the project-solet register and retires the lane through retire_session only where the Unit is proved terminal, so the finished lane's worktree is disposed of too. A lane whose Unit is unreadable or still in flight is left untouched with an advisory.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: considered is how many of the given rows were read. retired lists the rows driven through retire_session, each with agent_instance_id, unit_id, the unit_state that proved it terminal, already_retired, the resulting lifecycle_state and the recorded worktree_disposition; unit_state is empty for an already-retired row because no register read was made, and worktree_disposition names what happened to that lane's tree (removed, retained_not_disposable, retained_error or not_provisioned). advisories lists every row left exactly as it was, each naming the row and the reason. A row appears in exactly one of the two lists.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Report retired and advisories together: an advisory is a row deliberately left alone, not a failure, and the call is complete whether or not any row was eligible. Never describe an advisory row as retired, and never infer that an absent advisory means every lane was finished. Quote the reason text as given. A retained worktree_disposition means retire_session kept that lane's tree because it could not prove its bytes recoverable; report it rather than suggesting deletion. This verb introduces no new termination, disposal or lifecycle behaviour of its own.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Composes the existing retire_session once per eligible row. Eligibility needs positive proof: the register read must have completed for that row's own digest-verified assigned Unit and returned a terminal Unit state. A row that cannot be proved is skipped with an advisory, never retired and never failed, because retiring a lane is irreversible for its host. Already-retired rows pass through retire_session's own early return with no register read, so the whole call is safely re-drivable with the same instances.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: state_service_unavailable: the solet has no bound state service, so no row was read or changed. agent_instance_ids_required: the request did not carry agent_instance_ids as a list. session_not_found: one of the given agent_instance_ids names no managed_session row; no row was retired by this call. A per-row problem is never one of these codes - an unreadable register read, a Unit still working, an unsupported host or a lane whose bytes retire_session could not prove recoverable all arrive as advisory strings inside a completed result.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For session_not_found, list the fleet and re-request with instances that exist. For a row reported as advisory because its register read did not complete, check the configured psolet CLI and re-request; the row is unchanged and the call is safe to repeat. For a row whose Unit is still in flight, nothing is wrong: close the Unit in the register first, then re-request. For a row retire_session declined because the lane still holds unproved bytes, preserve those bytes by delivering the candidate or registering the exact document and re-request; never delete them to make the row eligible.
